step2.ptxt: If work on the airbag and pretensioner system is not performed using the correct procedures and methods, the system may deploy during work and cause a serious, life-threatening accident. Also, incorrect repairs may prevent the system from operating when necessary. When servicing (removal/installation, inspection, replacement of parts, etc.), read the following items carefully and perform work according to the correct procedures and methods described in this manual.
Before starting work, check the DTCs, then turn the IG OFF, disconnect the battery negative terminal and wait 90 seconds.

step3.ptxt: The airbag and pretensioner system is equipped with a back-up power source, so if work is started within 90 seconds of disconnecting the battery negative terminal, the airbag may deploy.
Since some systems' memory is cleared when the battery negative terminal is disconnected, record the memory contents of each system before work and reset them after work.

step1.ptxt: General Precautions for Airbags and Pretensioners

step2.ptxt: Use a Toyota electrical tester for electrical inspections.
Follow the instructions on the caution labels attached around the system.
Never disassemble.
If a part has been dropped, or has cracks, dents, chips or other deformation, replace it with a new genuine part.
Never use airbag and pretensioner parts from another vehicle; always install new parts when replacing.
Do not expose directly to high heat or flames.
Even if the airbag and pretensioner parts did not activate in a collision, perform an inspection using the diagnostic system.
Do not allow grease, cleaning agents, oil, water, etc. to adhere. If any adheres, immediately wipe it off with a dry cloth or equivalent.

Store and handle in a place free from high temperatures [ambient temperature of 93°C or higher for airbags (80°C or higher for pretensioners)] and high humidity, and not easily affected by electrical noise.
When scrapping a vehicle or disposing of a single part, always deploy it using SST.

step2.ptxt: Never measure the resistance of airbag and pretensioner parts.

atten2.ptxt: The tester current may cause the airbag or pretensioner to deploy, which is very dangerous.

step1.ptxt: Precautions for Disposal of Airbags and Pretensioners (Before Deployment)

step2.ptxt: Never dispose of the parts in an undeployed state.
Deploy airbags and pretensioners outdoors in a flat place where safety can be ensured. Also, avoid deployment in residential areas as much as possible.
Since the deployment of airbags and pretensioners is loud, notify everyone thoroughly in advance that deployment will be performed.
When deploying airbags and pretensioners, use SST and stay at least 5m away from the airbag and pretensioner.
Since static electricity may cause airbags and pretensioners to deploy, discharge static electricity beforehand by touching a water pipe, steel frame, etc. with bare hands.

atten3.ptxt: Since static electricity may cause airbags and pretensioners to deploy, discharge static electricity beforehand by touching a water pipe, steel frame, etc. with bare hands.

step2.ptxt: When deploying an airbag, be careful not to let the deployment surface face downward.

step1.ptxt: Precautions for Disposal of Airbags and Pretensioners (After Deployment)

step2.ptxt: Some areas of deployed airbags and pretensioners reach high temperatures of several hundred °C or more, so leave them for at least 30 minutes after deployment.
Do not apply water, etc. to deployed airbags and pretensioners.
When handling deployed airbags and pretensioners, wear dustproof protective goggles and gloves.
Place deployed airbags and pretensioners in a strong, transparent plastic bag, seal it and dispose of it.
Always wash your hands with water after completing work.

step1.ptxt: Precautions for Horn Button Assembly (Driver Airbag), Instrument Panel Passenger Airbag Assembly (Front Passenger Airbag), Front Seat Airbag Assembly, Curtain Shield Airbag and Instrument Panel Lower Airbag No.1

step2.ptxt: When removing even temporarily, such as during work, always store with the deployment surface facing upward.

atten2.ptxt: If the airbag deploys for any reason with the deployment surface facing down, a serious accident resulting in death may occur.

step2.ptxt: When storing, do not place objects on top of the airbag or stack airbags.

step1.ptxt: Precautions for Front Seat Outer Belt Assembly (Pretensioner)

step2.ptxt: When removing even temporarily, such as during work, do not touch the area around the belt retractor.

atten2.ptxt: If the pretensioner is activated for some reason and the belt is retracted, a serious, life-threatening accident may result.

step2.ptxt: When storing, do not place objects on the pretensioner or stack pretensioners.
Always center the spiral cable when installing the spiral cable and when removing/installing the steering wheel. (see )

atten3.ptxt: If the steering wheel is operated without centering, the spiral cable may break.

step1.ptxt: Precautions for Airbag Computer Assembly, Front Airbag Sensor, Side Airbag Sensor Assembly and Airbag Sensor Rear

step2.ptxt: If the airbags and pretensioners have deployed in a collision (including cases where only an airbag or only a pretensioner has deployed), always replace the sensor assemblies (airbag computer, front, side and rear sensors as a set).

step1.ptxt: Precautions for Wire Harness and Connector

step2.ptxt: Except for some parts in the engine room, the wire harnesses are all yellow.
Special connectors are used, so handle them with sufficient care.

step1.ptxt: Handling of Vehicles Damaged in a Collision, etc.

step2.ptxt: When using an electric welder, remove the airbags and pretensioners before starting work.
If there is a possibility of impact being applied to the airbag computer assembly, front airbag sensor, side airbag sensor assembly and airbag sensor rear, remove them beforehand.
Do not expose the airbag computer assembly, front airbag sensor, side airbag sensor assembly and airbag sensor rear to high temperatures.
Some areas of airbags and pretensioners reach high temperatures of several hundred °C or more when deployed, so check that the surrounding wire harnesses and connectors are not damaged or melted.
